correctness.rationale: The killed Brownian resolvent and no-reset absorption transform are explicit, yielding exact geometric-renewal joint Laplace and mixed-derivative covariance identities. Positive cost transforms give strict finite-rate covariance positivity. A resolvent split plus Potter domination gives B_j(r) asymptotics and an independently justified logarithmic q-derivative; inserting them into exact second-moment formulas yields the universal Pearson expression. Strict trigamma duplication and decrease establish the unique exponent optimum. Finite-rate resolvent quadratures, cross-differentiated transform checks and nonconstant slowly varying examples were executed successfully using the packaged checker; experiments do not substitute for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The central 2023 source already supplies the exact joint renewal Laplace transform, so that input is explicitly credited. The new contribution is the nontrivial weak-reset Pearson correlation limit for regularly varying cost functions and the strict sharp maximization at growth index one. Priority remains qualified by possible implicit derivability from more general uninspected work.

value.rationale: Recorded reset cost and first passage duration are jointly uncertain, and individual mean-cost or mean-search optima do not quantify their dependence. This theorem gives a universal cross-statistic independent of geometric/diffusive scales, a sharp meaningful maximizer at physically natural linear-distance return cost, and a strict finite-rate sign law. The assertion concerns a full regular-variation class and a motivated risk quantity, not a special numeric case.
